tools.name: nsd_publish
tools.description: Put a page online at <name>.nsd.sg. Give a site name and either the full HTML of the page or a list of files. Creates the site if you do not have it yet; on a site you already own it adds or replaces the given files and keeps the rest. Returns the live URL. IMPORTANT: if any file contains <script>,

tools.name: nsd_update
tools.description: Replace ALL files of an existing site with the given HTML or files. Older versions are kept and can be restored from the dashboard. Same rule as nsd_publish: anything containing <script>, on*= attributes or javascript: must be sent as files with encoding "base64", or the hosting firewall refuses it

tools.name: nsd_list_sites
tools.description: List the caller's sites: id, name, live URL, status, plan and days of free period left.

tools.name: nsd_get_site
tools.description: One site: URL, status, files, storage used and the plan's limits.

tools.name: nsd_read_file
tools.description: Read one file of a live site, exactly as it is online now. Use it before a small change ("change the price", "fix the date") in a chat that does not have the page yet: read the file, change only what the user asked, then send it back with nsd_publish under the same name. Text files come back as text

tools.name: nsd_delete_site
tools.description: Delete a site and all its versions. Requires the site id (never a name). The address becomes free for anyone.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "nsd_publish" is 1236 chars, far longer than this server's median (209). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "nsd_publish" stacks urgency/override words (important, always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: nsd_publish, nsd_list_sites, nsd_get_site, nsd_read_file · Private data: nsd_publish, nsd_update, nsd_get_site, nsd_read_file · Public sink: nsd_publish, nsd_read_file · Destructive: nsd_delete_site.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: nsd_publish, nsd_list_sites, nsd_get_site, nsd_read_file · Private data: nsd_publish, nsd_update, nsd_get_site, nsd_read_file · Public sink: nsd_publish, nsd_read_file · Destructive: nsd_delete_site

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
